system: Purified human Tyrosine-protein kinase Mer (Q12866) in vitro
readout: ADP-Glo luminescence proportional to kinase activity; percent inhibition derived from compound vs vehicle controls

steps.instruction: Prepare a 10-point serial dilution of CHEMBL1231206 in DMSO, plus vehicle-only, no-enzyme, no-compound (100% activity), and reference inhibitor controls.

parameters.top_concentration_uM: 30 (assumption; no packet evidence for this compound's potency range — contextual MER IC50s span ~2.9–1370 nM, so a 30 µM top with 3-fold dilution covers nM–µM)
parameters.vehicle_fraction: unresolved — maximum tolerated DMSO fraction not supported by packet; keep constant across all wells and below typical kinase-assay tolerance (assumption)

steps.instruction: Combine compound dilution, Mer kinase, tyrosine-containing substrate, and ATP in a 384-well plate using a Hepes-based buffer per the retained activity-assay conditions, and incubate.

parameters.buffer: 50 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 10 mM MgCl2, 1.0 mM DTT, 0.01% Triton X-100, 0.1% BSA, 50 µL final volume, 384-well polypropylene plate (evidence: CHEMBL5731805)
parameters.enzyme_concentration: unresolved — Mer enzyme concentration not stated in packet; must be titrated to give linear signal over the incubation window
parameters.substrate_concentration: 1.0 µM peptide substrate (contextual evidence: CHEMBL5731805 used 1.0 µM fluorescent substrate; substrate identity for Mer not specified — unresolved)
parameters.ATP_concentration: ATP at the Km of Mer (evidence: CHEMBL5731805); the numeric Km value is unresolved — determine experimentally
parameters.temperature: unresolved — not stated in packet; ambient/room temperature assumed (assumption)

steps.instruction: Stop the reaction, deplete residual ATP, run the ADP detection reaction, and read luminescence per the ADP-Glo manufacturer protocol.

parameters.stop_reagent: 20 µL of 70 mM EDTA is supported as a stop for the analogous assay (evidence: CHEMBL5731805); ADP-Glo-specific reagent volumes, depletion_time, and detection_time are unresolved — no packet evidence; follow vendor protocol (assumption)

steps.instruction: Normalize luminescence to vehicle (100% activity) and no-enzyme (0% activity) controls, fit percent inhibition vs log10 concentration with a four-parameter logistic model, and report IC50 with 95% CI.

parameters.fit_model: 4-parameter logistic (top/bottom constrained or free per fit quality)
parameters.acceptance_criteria: unresolved — no packet-supported criteria; propose (assumption): vehicle-control CV <20%, reference inhibitor within historical range, Z' > 0.5

controls: Reference Mer inhibitor control (identity unresolved — no specific reference named in packet)
rationale: The question asks for biochemical inhibition of purified Mer kinase, so the kinase step cards (kinase-prepare/react/detect/analyse) are used and the cell-viability cards are excluded. The ADP-Glo luminescence readout directly measures kinase activity and is mechanistically distinct from cellular ATP viability. Reaction buffer, volume, substrate concentration, ATP-at-Km strategy, 180 min incubation, and EDTA stop are supported by the retained Mer activity assay CHEMBL5731805 (document CHEMBL5725982). The concentration series (30 µM top, 3-fold, 10 points, triplicates) is an assumption chosen to span the wide contextual MER IC50 range (2.9 nM–1.37 µM from CHEMBL4433481, CHEMBL4189001, CHEMBL5731805) without asserting any potency for CHEMBL1231206. This experiment establishes biochemical inhibition only; it does not by itself demonstrate cellular target engagement or viability effects.
limitations: No potency measurement for CHEMBL1231206 exists in the packet; the top concentration and dilution scheme are assumptions, not sourced facts.
Mer enzyme concentration, numeric ATP Km, substrate identity, reaction temperature, and DMSO tolerance are unresolved — not supported by packet evidence.

ADP-Glo reagent volumes, depletion time, and detection time are unsupported; the retained assay CHEMBL5731805 used a LabChip mobility-shift readout, not ADP-Glo, so detection parameters must come from the vendor protocol.
The EDTA stop is cited from a different readout format; compatibility with ADP-Glo chemistry should be verified.
Retained IC50 values are contextual for other compounds and must not be used to estimate CHEMBL1231206 potency.
Biochemical inhibition does not establish target-specific causality in cells; a separate cellular target-engagement or viability experiment would be required and is not designed here.
